title: Activation Lifecycle Decision Canvas: Remote Hire Intake, Interview Rubric & 21-day Accelerator
body:
Purpose:
This canvas defines a repeatable pathway for remote hires (including contractors moving to perm) focused on fast, equitable decisions and a friction-minimized first 21 days. It bundles: a shortlist prioritization heuristic, an interview rubric tuned for cross-functional pods, bias mitigation checkpoints, and a micro-onboarding accelerator with explicit signals to convert/extend/terminate.

Scope:
- Role types: IC (IC1-IC5), Eng Managers, SRE, Product, Solutions Eng, Customer Success.
- Hiring modes: full-time remote, contractor (3mo->perm), lateral transfers, relocation optional.
- Geography: timezone-aware scheduling for NA/EU/APAC candidates.

High-level SLA (target):
- Requisition posted -> first screen scheduled: 3 business days
- Interview loop complete: 10 business days
- Offer decision to candidate: 2 business days after final debrief
- Preboarding checklist triggered on offer accept: within 24 hours

Roles & RACI (short):
- Hiring manager: defines role outcomes, scores final rubric, owns offer.
- Interview coordinator (people-ops): schedules, timezone logistics, candidate comms.
- Interview panel: completes rubric, surfaces risks.
- People-ops lead: gatekeeper on compensation parity and IRL/perf budget.
- Eng-systems/tech lead: validates technical bar for role-specific hires.

Candidate Intake & Shortlisting Heuristic (score out of 100):
- Core skills match (40): resume keywords + sample work + role-specific test
- Impact & context (20): breadth/depth of prior outcomes, measurable impact
- Bar raising potential (15): indicators of learning velocity, mentorship, system-level thinking
- Culture fit signals (10): collaboration examples, customer empathy
- Logistics risk (15): visa/timezone/notice period (negative weight where relevant)
Pass threshold = 65 to move to interview loop.

Interview Loop Design (target 3–4 interviews / 90–120 mins total):
1) Hiring manager screen (30–40m): role expectations, past impact, signals for ramp
2) Technical deep-dive (40–50m): system design or take-home review (role dependent)
3) Product/behavioral (30m): collaboration, tradeoffs, communication
4) Optional pairing / live debugging (30m) for hands-on roles
All panels must submit rubric within 24 hours of interview.

Interview Rubric (1–5 each; 5 = clearly exceeds / hire now, 3 = meets, 1 = fails):
- Technical competence: mastery of fundamentals, domain libs, algorithms (weight 0.30)
- System thinking & design: tradeoff articulation, scalability, failure modes (weight 0.25)
- Problem solving & debugging: structured approach, tests, failure recovery (weight 0.15)
- Communication & collaboration: clarity, cross-team empathy, async docs (weight 0.15)
- Role-specific craft: e.g., embeddings/infra/observability proficiency (weight 0.10)
- Growth mindset & learning signals: coachability, prior learning velocity (weight 0.05)
Total score normalized to 100. Minimum panel average = 3.5 and aggregate >= 70 recommended for offer.

Sample behavioral probes (timing short):
- "Tell me about a time you shipped a feature when dependencies were unclear. How did you decide what to own?"
- "Describe an outage you debugged end-to-end. What was your hypothesis pruning process?"
- "When you disagreed with a PM/peer, how did you resolve it and what changed as a result?"

Technical deep-dive example prompts:
- Service / runtime role: "Design a KV cache layer for prompt-serving at 500 RPS with 8–16K token windows. Outline caching policy, eviction, and KV cache sharding tradeoffs."
- Infra/SRE role: "You see token-latency P95 drift after model rollout. List investigative steps, metrics/queries to run, and possible mitigations."
- Data/Research role: "Given a new embedding model with lower cost but slightly higher retrieval noise, design an A/B evaluation for production migration."

Bias mitigation checkpoints:
- Standardized rubric and mandatory unbiased example anchor responses for each score band
- Diverse panel requirement: at least one interviewer outside hiring subteam
- Candidate blind components (code exercise without resume metadata) where feasible
- Calibration sessions once per quarter to re-align scoring across teams

Decision gates & outcomes:
- Hire (offer): candidate >= threshold, positive manager recommendation, compensation aligned
- Hold for additional evidence: panel median between 3.0–3.5 or single competency below threshold -> require targeted take-home or follow-up pairing assignment within 4 business days
- No hire: median <= 2.5 or negative red-flag (integrity/communication)

Offer templates & quick scripts (people-ops):
- Rapid verbal offer script (2m) covering base, equity, start window, manager intro
- Follow-up email template link: GITHUB-PR-ops/templates/offer-email
- Decline + feedback: brief strengths + 1 area for growth; offer loop to reapply in 6 months if appropriate

21-day Accelerator (micro-onboarding) — Purpose: compress time-to-contribution while surfacing fit signals early.
Preboarding (on accept, Day 0):
- Accesses: GitHub, Slack, internal wiki, infra staging project, ticketing
- Hardware & accounts: coordinate with IT within 24h of acceptance
- Welcome packet: org chart, key intents for 30/60/90, paired buddy assignment

Week 1 (Day 1–7) - Orientation + shallow dives:
- Day 1: team meet & greet, cadence overview, 1:1 with manager for success plan
- Day 2–3: system walkthroughs (runtime, infra, evals), shadow a runbook incident postmortem
- Day 4–5: small ownerable task (bugfix / doc contribution) assigned with pair mentor

Signals week1 (pass/fail):
- Completed task with tests or docs and merged PR OR identified blockers with plan
- Communication responsiveness across async channels

Week 2 (Day 8–14) - Ownership stretch:
- Ownerable feature slice or infra change with measurable outcome (low-risk)
- Scheduled mid-accelerator sync w/ manager and buddy to review progress

Signals week2:
- Demonstrated end-to-end delivery or clear technical plan and execution milestones
- Evidence of effective collaboration (PR reviews, cross-team tickets)

Week 3 (Day 15–21) - Impact & evaluation:
- Deliverable accepted to mainline or operational handoff documented
- Manager gathers panel feedback from buddy, peer owners, and product partner

End-of-accelerator decision rubric (convert / extend / offboard):
- Convert to perm: met 80%+ of signals across weeks, team recommendation positive, no unresolved conduct issues
- Extend probation (30d): mixed signals, requires closer ramp-up or role calibration
- Offboard: pattern of major gaps in core competencies or integrity/red-flag behavior

Probation evidence checklist (to accompany final recommendation):
- 3 artifacts: merged PR or design doc, customer/peer feedback note, oncall/runbook contribution
- 1:1 manager narrative: evidence mapped to rubric competencies

Timezone & logistics playbook (practical tips):
- Default interview windows per region: NA 9am–2pm PT, EU 10am–4pm CET, APAC 8am–12pm SGT
- Compensate for odd-hours interviews: offer a $50 meal/delivery stipend for interviews >2 hours total where candidate travels significant timezones (documented local law permitting)
- Staggered start schedules: prefer mid-week start for ramp-friendly onboarding activities

Edge cases & special flows:
- Contractor->Perm: require 30-day evidence during contractor engagement with early check-ins at day 14 and day 28 to capture conversion signals. Standard conversion template to be used for comp parity and role leveling review.
- Executive/org hires: separate panel with senior leadership + extended reference set and 2-week onboarding concierge
- Visa-relocation hires: add relocation & legal checklist and extended offer acceptance window; coordinate with finance for tax implications

Operational notes for people-ops team:
- Maintain a public registry (sheet) of active requisitions and stage timestamps (auto-updated via ATS webhook)
- Run weekly truncated calibration digest: 5 recent hires with anonymized rubrics + calibration score delta
- Quarterly retrospective: gather hiring velocity, cancel rates, conversion by recruiter, time-to-offer metrics

Open questions / follow-ups (work-in-progress):
- Should we standardize a single take-home exercise across eng IC levels vs role-specific tasks? Tradeoffs: consistency vs relevance.
- Compensation parity: acceptance of market-based outlier offers for strategic senior hires—who signs off? (people-ops lead + CFO delegation?)
- Pilot stipend policy for late interviews in APAC/EMEA—budget and tax implications to confirm with finance/legal.

Appendix: quick scoring cheat-sheet (example):
- Candidate A: Tech 4, System 4, Debug 4, Comm 3, Craft 3, Growth 4 -> weighted = 4*0.3 + 4*0.25 + 4*0.15 + 3*0.15 + 3*0.1 + 4*0.05 = 3.75 -> normalized 75 -> offer
- Candidate B: Tech 3, System 3, Debug 2, Comm 4, Craft 3, Growth 3 -> weighted = 3.05 -> normalized 61 -> hold/request follow-up

Notes to reviewers: This doc is intended to be a living canvas. If you modify the rubric bands or signal list, please increment the version footer and add a short rationale in the change log section of the Confluence page linked above.
